# dsh-system-prompt-studio

A **DeepSeek Harness** plugin that lets you inspect and override the
**system prompt** a conversatio

n actually sends to the model — per conversation, at runtime, without
restarting.
DSH itself only exposes deployment-wide persona prefix/suffix in configuration files: change one and

you
need a restart, and it affects every session. This plugin moves the same capability to runtime,

per
session, effective immediately.
> 中文说明见文末 · 跳转到中文
## What it does
- **See the real thing.** The panel shows the system prompt your conversation *actually sent* on its

last request, plus the section list that was assembled for it (name / order / character count).
- *
*Override it three ways.**
| Mode | Effect |

| **Append** (default) | Keeps every first-party section, adds yours at the end. Safest. |
| **Repla

ce a section** | Shadows one named first-party section, e.g. `deployment:persona-suffix`. |
| **Repl
ace everything** | Your text becomes the entire system prompt. Highest risk — see below. |

- **Applies on the next model request.** No restart, no reload.
- **Persists per session**, and a **

global default** applies to new conversations automatically.
- **Inherits across forks.** A forked c

onversation picks up its parent's rules along the `parentSession`
chain, with a **Pin** action to fr

eeze the inherited result locally.
- **Guards unsaved edits.** Esc, backdrop click and the close but

ton all ask before discarding.
- **Zero runtime dependencies.** Only Node built-ins; it does not imp
ort any `@deepseek-ai/*` package.
### ⚠️ Before you use "Replace everything"
That mode removes **all** first-party guidance — tool instructions, structured-output rules, plan-mo

de
policy. Tool-calling quality can drop noticeably. Runtime context (working directory, sandbox pol

icy,
approval policy) is still sent as a user-side snapshot and is **not** replaced by your text.
Also: assembly allows only one active `complete` section. If another plugin registers one in the sam

e
session, assembly fails with `multiple complete prompt sections`. Switch back to Append or Replace

ssembly fails with `multiple complete prompt sections`. Switch back to Append or Replace to
recover.
## Requirements

- DSH `>=0.2.2-0 <0.3.0-0` (Web and Desktop share the same client artifact)
- Node.js ≥ 22.19.0
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Replace `<profile>` with your profile name — for the Web build that is usually `web`.
**Pin a commit for reproducibility.** Without a ref you get whatever is on the default branch, so an

y
later push changes what you install next time:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Local directory install (for development)
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### If pnpm blocks the build script
pnpm refuses to run build scripts from Git dependencies by default. This plugin's `prepare` script o

nly
**verifies** that the entry files exist — it compiles nothing and writes nothing — so being bloc

ked does
not break the install. If pnpm stops anyway, it writes a pending entry into your profile's
`pnpm-workspace.yaml`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Set it to `true` and re-run the same `add` command.
> ⚠️ That grants this package's code permission to run **outside the DSH agent sandbox** at install

time.
> Here, `scripts/verify-entry.mjs` only reads files — no network, no writes —
> but grant it o
nly to source you trust.
### After installing
The Host half activates immediately. **The client half is new JavaScript, so refresh the page once**

to
make the title-bar button appear.
Verify the Host half is live:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A `{"ok":true,...,"capability":{...}}` response means it's working.
### Uninstall
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Your saved overrides are **not** deleted.
## Usage

1. A **System prompt** button appears in the title bar of any conversation (with a dot when this
con

versation already has its own override). On a **brand-new conversation** the title bar is
hidden by

the harness, so the button lives in the welcome area instead, labeled
**Set system prompt**.
2. Pick

a scope: **this conversation** or **global default**. The global default applies to top-level
conve

rsations only — not to subagents.
[该节后续省略]
## Known limitations
1. **Overrides are keyed by session id, but forks inherit.** A forked conversation picks up the near

est
ancestor's rules (disable with `inheritOnFork`). Subagents do not take the global default and do

not
participate in the chain. Resuming a session under the same id re-applies its rules.
2. **Cold

sessions** (no live agent) can be saved for, but take effect once resumed. Inheritance
specifically

requires a live agent, because the parent chain is read from the session header — a cold
session has

none until it is running again.
3. **`{{…}}` is not interpolated.** Bodies are registered with `int

erpolate: false`, so braces stay
literal. This is deliberate: otherwise any `{{x}}` in your text wou

ld fail assembly with
*unknown prompt variable*.
4. **Cache prefix invalidation.** Changing the syst

em prompt invalidates that conversation's provider
cache from the first changed token, so the next r

equest pays for the new prefix. That is how the
mechanism works, not plugin behaviour.
5. **"Replace

everything" is exclusive.** Assembly permits a single active `complete` section.
6. **Section attri

bution is approximate.** The list is attributed via the assembly context's scope (the
agent); if tha

t is unavailable it falls back to the most recent assembly. Overrides themselves are
unaffected.
## Privacy
No credentials, API keys, conversation content or personal paths are in this repository. At runtime

the
plugin writes only under your own `$DSH_HOME/dsh-system-prompt-studio/`. Nothing is sent anywher

e
plugin writes only under your own `$DSH_HOME/dsh-system-prompt-studio/`. Nothing is sent anywhere.
